name: Mike Pence
role: U.S. Representative (2001-2013), Governor of Indiana (2013-2017), Vice President (2017-2021); leads Advancing American Freedom
summary: A social and fiscal conservative and evangelical Christian who opposes abortion and same-sex marriage, favors low taxes, entitlement reform, school choice and a strong military. He has supported free trade and NATO and backed Ukraine, and since 2021 has broken with Trump over the 2020 election, tariffs and Ukraine.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted against the ACA (2009 House bill, 2010 concurrence) and for its repeal in 2011 and 2012, and in 2017 called for a health system based on personal responsibility and free-market competition instead.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted against the Fair Minimum Wage Act in January 2007, the bill raising the federal minimum to $7.25.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: As vice-president-elect he said he and Trump 'believe fervently in the free market' and blamed taxes, regulation and big government for stifling competitiveness.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Voted repeatedly to repeal the estate tax permanently (2001, 2002, 2003, 2005, 2006).

unions-good.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Voted against Dodd-Frank, refused to comply with EPA rules, and as a candidate pledged to reverse Biden-era regulatory orders.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted for the 2005 Patriot Act reauthorization, the Protect America Act (2007), the FISA Amendments Act (2008), its 2012 extension and the 2011 Patriot Act extension.

legalize-drugs.rationale: As governor he said in 2014, 'I don't support legalization of marijuana and that's been my position for a long time'; he spoke only to marijuana, so the answer is not stronger.

limit-guns.rationale: Told the NRA in 2018 that the right to keep and bear arms 'will not be infringed', calling it one of the most important freedoms, and urged states to let school staff carry concealed weapons.

empower-police-military.rationale: Pushed a dramatic defense spending increase as vice president, vowed to reverse a defense spending cut, and opposed defunding police.

decide-locally.rationale: He voted against No Child Left Behind (2001, s13) and criticised its federal expansion, but that is education policy only, narrower than this statement; no general position verified.

rehabilitation.rationale: Voted for the Second Chance Act on prisoner reentry (2007), but as governor signed 2016 non-suspendible ten-year minimums for repeat meth and heroin dealers, saying drug strategy 'must start with enforcement'.

traditional-family.rationale: The earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia or OnTheIssues; the original source was not checked in this pass, so no verified position. His recorded words defend 'traditional marriage' (s20), which is narrower than this statement.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Argued on CNN in 2004 for a national constitutional amendment 'to defend marriage' against same-sex marriage, and voted for the federal marriage amendment in 2004 and 2006.

abortion-legal.rationale: Signed Indiana HEA 1337 (2016), supported overturning Roe, and in June 2023 urged every GOP candidate to back a nationwide ban before 15 weeks as a minimum.

more-religion-public.rationale: Calls religious freedom America's first freedom, backed repealing the Johnson Amendment and restoring religious protections in federal contracting.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia or OnTheIssues; the original source was not checked in this pass, so no verified position.

free-trade.rationale: Voted for CAFTA-DR (2005) and the Korea, Colombia and Panama agreements (2011), and in 2025 called Trump's broad tariffs the largest peacetime tax increase.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: In the 2016 debate he said the US should be prepared to strike Assad regime military targets to stop the humanitarian crisis in Aleppo and to protect safe zones with a no-fly zone.

open-borders.rationale: Voted for the 2005 Border Protection and Illegal Immigration Control Act and the 2006 Secure Fence Act.

limit-growth.rationale: Champions growth through tax cuts and an all-of-the-above energy strategy; rejects climate limits on the economy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Voted against the 2009 cap-and-trade bill (American Clean Energy and Security Act) and for the 2011 Energy Tax Prevention Act blocking EPA greenhouse-gas rules.

central-planning.rationale: His fervent stated belief in the free market, against big government stifling the economy, contradicts the claim that central planning can work better.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted for permanent estate-tax repeal bills in 2001, 2002, 2003, 2005 and 2006; voted against the 2009 bill that would have kept the tax at 2009 levels.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In 2025 argued tariffs are paid by importers and consumers and called the broad reciprocal tariffs a peacetime tax hike, while backing China-specific tariffs as VP; recent view leans against.

military-superiority.rationale: Backed a $716B defense increase, a Space Force and a dramatic military buildup against China and Russia as VP, and wanted a defense cut reversed in his 2024 plan.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia or OnTheIssues; the original source was not checked in this pass, so no verified position.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Praised the Truman-era Democrats for helping 'create the state of Israel' (2019) and in 2002 backed Israel as an ally 'since 1948' in its West Bank operations.

school-vouchers.rationale: As governor he signed the 2013 expansion of Indiana's Choice Scholarship voucher programme, saying students deserve every opportunity and families more options.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted against the 2009 stimulus bill (HR 1) on passage and on the conference report, backing Republican alternatives.

reason-over-faith.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Called Indiana a pro-coal state, backed Keystone XL and ANWR drilling, and pledged to reverse Biden energy orders and expand oil and gas leasing.

separated-powers.rationale: In his Jan. 6, 2021 letter said his oath barred him from unilaterally deciding electoral votes, and his group has urged Congress to reclaim tariff authority.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said in 2017 that the US 'strongly supports NATO' and will be unwavering in its commitment, and in 2019 described the transatlantic alliance as being defended and renewed.

death-penalty.rationale: On Face the Nation in 2023 he called for 'an expedited federal death penalty' for mass shooters so they 'meet their fate in months, not years'.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: In a 2002 House floor speech he asked that evolution be taught 'not as fact, but as theory' and that schools 'consider teaching other theories of the origin of species', naming the belief of the Declaration's signers.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Signed Indiana RFRA in 2015 and later backed religious protections in federal contracting; opposed reading RFRA as license for discrimination but backed exemptions.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia or OnTheIssues; the original source was not checked in this pass, so no verified position.

collective-defense.rationale: Spoke of renewing NATO allies' 'commitment to our common defense' (2019) and an unwavering US commitment to NATO (2017); he did not address Article 5 by name.

flat-income-tax.rationale: News reports (e.g. HuffPost, 2010) quote a Detroit Economic Club speech calling for a flat tax, but the speech text was not found, so the quotation could not be checked in the original: no verified position.

space-expansion.rationale: As head of the National Space Council he set a goal of returning Americans to the Moon within five years, building a permanent base and going on to Mars, and called it a duty to make American values the foundation of 'mankind's future in space'.

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted against TARP (2008) and the auto-industry rescue, and said in 2009 that AIG and taxpayers would have been better off with an orderly bankruptcy than a 'massive government bailout'.

patriotic-education.rationale: His 2022 Freedom Agenda promoted "patriotic" education with heavier testing on the founding documents; it names no flag or anthem requirement.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: In April 2015 he signed the RFRA clarification bill stating the law does not authorize refusing service, housing or jobs over sexual orientation.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Said foreign investment benefits America but cited strengthened CFIUS review in his China speech.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: In 2004 he backed giving younger workers 'personal savings accounts' and letting them invest a portion of their payroll taxes, while keeping promised benefits for current retirees; a partial carve-out, not a full replacement.

single-official-language.rationale: The earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia or OnTheIssues; the original source was not checked in this pass, so no verified position.

corporate-influence.rationale: The earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia or OnTheIssues; the original source was not checked in this pass, so no verified position. His 2002 vote against McCain-Feingold (s13) concerns campaign-finance rules, not whether corporations have too much influence.

non-intervention.rationale: Supported the Iraq war, Libya action, and arming Ukraine against Russia.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Champions US membership of NATO and warned allies against depending on Russia for energy or buying adversaries' weapons.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Voted against the Don't Ask, Don't Tell Repeal Act in December 2010.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: In his 2018 NRA speech he praised an armed citizen who killed an attacker, and said guns give every American the power to defend themselves and their families.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Voted for the 2002 Iraq war authorization and against the 2007 Iraq redeployment bills, and in 2016 backed strikes on Assad regime targets.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Voted against the 2009 cap-and-trade bill that would have priced carbon emissions.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Told the NRA in 2018 that firearms in law-abiding citizens' hands make communities safer and called the Second Amendment the 'great equalizer' for self-defence.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted for the 2011 balanced budget amendment and the Cut, Cap and Balance Act; he voted against the 2009 Statutory PAYGO Act.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia or OnTheIssues; the original source was not checked in this pass, so no verified position.

voter-id.rationale: In 2026 he urged the Senate to make voter ID the law in all 50 states and to require photo ID or proof of citizenship at the ballot box; his 2022 Freedom Agenda also called for voter ID at the polls.

close-ties-china.rationale: His 2018 Hudson speech set out a confrontational China policy: tariffs, security and human-rights criticism, and rejection of reliance on Beijing.

multipolar-world.rationale: Champions American leadership of the free world and says Putin only understands strength.

notes: Recent clear positions govern: he opposes Trump's broad 2025 tariffs but backed China tariffs as VP. As governor he accepted Obergefell as law while personally keeping his traditional-marriage view. Many entries rely on secondary catalogs of his votes and statements; most votes are medium confidence. Opus pass 2026-10-31: re-sourced answers that cited only Wikipedia/OnTheIssues to the House roll-call record (Voteview), the MediaSum CNN/NPR transcripts and his own speeches, nulling those that could not be traced to an original. Searched line 12 topics: guns and self-defence (NRA 2018 speech), political violence (his Jan. 6, 2021 'violence never wins' remarks condemn a specific attack, left null), China influence and the Great Firewall (Hudson 2018: no settled position on foreign-funding limits or shutdowns), NATO. His Libya votes in 2011 were split (against both authorizing and defunding the mission). Second Opus round (same day): re-traced the nulled answers in MediaSum (CNN/NPR), the Congressional Record and Indiana reporting: marijuana, Social Security accounts, the 2002 evolution speech and 2016 mandatory minimums found; flat tax (2010 speech text not found), traditional family, union membership, official language, UN power, equal outcomes, precautionary principle and corporate influence stay null. Line 14: space (National Space Council 2019) answered; searched Electoral College, term limits, international criminal courts and trade deficit without a settled position.
